newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-RODMAN WILL PLAY GAMES FOR FREE, NEWSPAPER SAYS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-RODMAN WILL PLAY GAMES FOR FREE, NEWSPAPER SAYS.

text.p: Dennis Rodman, suspended for 11 games and fined $25,000 in a kicking incident, will give up his paycheck from a number of games when he returns to the court, it was reported Friday.

The Chicago Sun-Times quoted the agent for the Chicago Bulls star as saying a "significant" number of games would be involved and that the money -- about $109,000 per game -- would go to charity or be returned to the team.
"I'll be back stronger than ever," Rodman told the newspaper.
"I'm working out twice a day. I'm going to stay in shape. But when I come back I'm going to do something else that no player has ever done. I'm going to play for free," he said.
"I feel I owe that to the Bulls," the five-time NBA rebounding king added.
In a game last week in Minneapolis, Rodman stumbled out of bounds, tripping over cameraman Eugene Amos and kicking at him as he got up off the floor.
Amos, in a delayed reaction, slumped over for more than five minutes before he was carried off and taken to a hospital.
Rodman was suspended for at least 11 games without pay, fined $25,000 and ordered to see a counsellor. He also agreed to pay the cameraman $200,000 in an out-of-court settlement.
In a television interview earlier in the week Rodman said he kicked at the man's camera and not at his groin, calling the contact a mere "tap."
